source_text: {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἐλέγομεν· μεμνήσομαι γάρ. {ΚΥΡ.} Θέα δὴ οὖν ὅτι καταφοιτῆσαν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ πῦρ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον, καταλήγειν οὐκ ἐᾷ, οὐδὲ οἷον ἀπανίστασθαι μαρανθὲν, ἀλλ' εἶναί τε διὰ παντὸς αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀπαύστως ἐμφιλοχωρεῖν. Μεμαρτύρηκε δὲ καὶ ὁ Βαπτιστὴς Ἰωάννης περὶ Χριστοῦ· «Ὅτι τεθέαμαι τὸ Πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐν εἴδει περιστερᾶς, καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐπ' αὐτόν. Καὶ ἐγὼ,» φησὶν, «οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν· ἀλλ' ὁ πέμψας με βαπτίζειν, αὐτός μοι εἶπεν· Ἐφ' ὃν ἂν [ε]ἴδῃς τὸ Πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ μένον ἐπ' αὐτὸν, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν Πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ.» Ἀνετυποῦτο δὴ οὖν ὡς ἐν σκιαῖς ἔτι τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἐν εἴδει πυρὸς καταβαῖνον ἐπὶ Χριστὸν, καὶ ἀεὶ μένον ἐπ' αὐτόν. Ἀκατεύναστον γὰρ καὶ ἀκατάληκτον παντελῶς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τὸ πῦρ. Ὅτι δὲ τῇ τοῦ πυρὸς φύσει τὸ Πνεῦμα παρεικάζεται, πληροφορεῖ σε λέγων τοῖς Ἰουδαίων δήμοις καὶ ὁ μακάριος Βαπτιστής· «Ἐγὼ βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι, μέσος δὲ ὑμῶν ἕστηκεν, ὂν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε, ὁ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος ἵνα λύσω αὐτοῦ τὸν ἱμάντα τοῦ ὑποδήματος.» Ἔφη δὲ, ὅτι «Αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν Πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί.» Βεβαπτίσμεθα γὰρ οὐκ εἰς πῦρ αἰσθητὸν, ἀλλ' ἐν ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, πυρὸς δίκην ἐκτήκοντι τὸν ἐν ψυχαῖς μολυσμόν, τοιγάρ τοι καὶ γέγραπται περὶ Χριστοῦ, ὅτι «Ἰδοὺ αὐτὸς εἰσπορεύεται ὡς πῦρ χωνευτηρίου, καὶ ὡς πόα πλυνόντων· καὶ καθιεῖται χωνεύων καὶ καθαρίζων, ὡς τὸ ἀργύριον καὶ ὡς τὸ χρυσίον.» Ἄσβεστον οὖν ἄρα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τὸ πῦρ. Μεμένηκε γὰρ ἐν Χριστῷ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, καίτοι κατὰ φύσιν ἐνυπάρχον αὐτῷ, καθὸ νοεῖται καὶ ἔστι Θεός. Ἔφη δὲ καὶ νόμος, ἴδιον τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τὸ πῦρ. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ γέγονεν ἄνθρωπος ὁ Μονογενὴς, καὶ κατά γε τὸ πρέπον τῇ ἀνθρωπότητι σχῆμα, καὶ ἐν μεθέξει Πνεύματος γεγενῆσθαι λέγεται· ἀλλ' οὖν αὐτοῦ τε καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἴδιον ἀληθῶς τὸ Πνεῦμά ἐστιν. Εἰ δὲ δή τις ἕλοιτο, τὸν ἐπὶ τῷδε λόγον καὶ ἐφ' ἕκαστον ἄγειν τῶν ἡγιασμένων διὰ πίστεως ἐν Χριστῷ, ὡς ἤδη πως αὐτὸν καὶ θεῖον νοεῖσθαι θυσιαστήριον· ἐπωφελὴς ὁ λόγος· πρέπει γὰρ, ἄνδρας τοὺς ἱεροὺς, καὶ Χριστῷ τὴν οἰκείαν ἀναθέντας ζωὴν, θερμοὺς καὶ ζέοντας ὁρᾶσθαι τῷ Πνεύματι, καὶ τοῦτο διὰ παντὸς, οὐκ εἰς ἀπόψυξιν καταφερομένους διὰ κοσμικῶν ἡδονῶν, ἀναζωπυροῦντας δὲ μᾶλλον ἐν ἁγιασμῷ τὸν νοῦν εἰς φιλοθεΐαν καὶ ἔφεσιν ἀρετῆς. Λατρείας γὰρ οὗτος τῆς λογικῆς ὁ τρόπος. Οὗτος μὲν οὖν ὁ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου λόγος. Προσεπιτάττει δέ τι καὶ τῇ ἱστορίᾳ χρήσιμον. Τὴν γάρ τοι σποδιὰν ἐκκομίζεσθαι δεῖν, οὐ παρ' ἑτέρου, φησὶ, τῶν ἀλλογενῶν, ἤγουν ἐξ ἑτέρας ὄντος φυλῆς, δι' ὑπουργίας δὲ μᾶλλον τῶν ἡγιασμένων. Ἐπιτήρει δὲ, ὅπως οὐδὲν ἡγεῖσθαι βραχὺ τῶν εἰς θείαν ἡκόντων λειτουργίαν ἀφίησιν ὁ νόμος, οὐδὲ οἷον ἱερατικῆς αὐτουργίας ἀνάξιον, ὡς παραχωρεῖν ἑτέρῳ μὴ ἱερῷ· οὐ γάρ τοι βάσιμα τοῖς ἀνάγνοις τὰ ἅγια. Ἀνέπαφον δὲ καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ θεῖόν
pass_a_gloss: PALL: we were saying (ἐλέγομεν); for I shall remember (μεμνήσομαι). CYR: see (θέα) that fire having come down (καταφοιτῆσαν) from heaven upon the altar (θυσιαστήριον) [he/the law] does not allow (ἐᾷ) to cease (καταλήγειν), nor as it were to depart (ἀπανίστασθαι) having withered (μαρανθέν), but to be through all [time] on it and unceasingly to dwell fondly (ἐμφιλοχωρεῖν). John the Baptist has testified (μεμαρτύρηκε) about Christ: I have beheld the Spirit descending from heaven in form (εἴδει) of dove and it remained (ἔμεινεν) on him; and I did not know him, but the one having sent me to baptize said: on whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining (μένον), this is the one baptizing in Holy Spirit [John 1:32-33]. So was typed out (ἀνετυποῦτο) as in shadows still the Holy Spirit, in form of fire descending on Christ and ever remaining. For un lulled (ἀκατεύναστον) and unceasing (ἀκατάληκτον) wholly the fire of the altar. That the Spirit is likened (παρεικάζεται) to the nature of fire, the blessed Baptist assures (πληροφορεῖ) you, saying to the crowds (δήμοις) of Jews: I baptize in water; in midst of you stands one whom you do not know, the one coming after me, of whom I am not worthy to loose the strap of sandal [John 1:26-27]; and said: he will baptize you in Holy Spirit and fire [Matt 3:11]. For we have been baptized not into perceptible (αἰσθητόν) fire but in Holy Spirit, by way of fire melting out (ἐκτήκοντι) the defilement (μολυσμόν) in souls; therefore written about Christ: behold he enters as fire of smelting furnace (χωνευτηρίου) and as herb of washers (πόα πλυνόντων); and he will sit smelting and cleansing as silver and gold [Mal 3:2-3 LXX]. Unquenchable (ἄσβεστον) then the fire. For the Holy Spirit has remained in Christ, although by nature (κατὰ φύσιν) being present in (ἐνυπάρχον) him, inasmuch as he is conceived and is God. And law said the fire [is] proper (ἴδιον) to the altar. For even if the Only begotten (Μονογενής) became man, and according to the form (σχῆμα) befitting humanity is said to have come to be in participation (μεθέξει) of Spirit, yet the Spirit is both his and in him and truly his own (ἴδιον). If someone should choose to apply the word to each of those sanctified (ἡγιασμένων) through faith in Christ, as already somehow he too being conceived as divine altar, profitable (ἐπωφελής) the word; for it befits holy men, having dedicated (ἀναθέντας) their own life to Christ, to be seen warm and boiling (ζέοντας) in the Spirit, and this always, not carried down into cooling (ἀπόψυξιν) through worldly pleasures, but rather rekindling (ἀναζωπυροῦντας) in sanctification (ἁγιασμῷ) the mind unto love of God (φιλοθεΐαν) and longing (ἔφεσιν) of virtue. For this the manner of rational worship (λατρείας λογικῆς). This then the word of the altar. He further commands (προσεπιτάττει) something useful also for the history (ἱστορίᾳ, literal level): the ash (σποδιάν) must be carried out not by another, he says, of the foreigners (ἀλλογενῶν), that is being of another tribe, but through service (ὑπουργίας) of the sanctified. Watch how the law lets nothing of things pertaining to divine liturgy be thought small, nor as it were unworthy of priestly own handiwork (αὐτουργίας), so as to yield to another not holy; for not walkable/accessible (βάσιμα) to the impure (ἀνάγνοις) the holy things. Untouchable (ἀνέπαφον) also the divine [altar itself; sentence completes in col. 824].
pass_b_english: Palladius: We did say so; I will keep it in mind.

Cyril: Consider, then, that the law does not allow the fire that came down from heaven upon the altar to die down, or, as it were, to fade and go away, but has it stay on the altar always and make its home there without ceasing (Leviticus 6:12–13). And John the Baptist bore witness about Christ: ‘I have seen the Spirit descending from heaven in the form of a dove, and it remained on him. And I did not know him,’ he says, ‘but he who sent me to baptize said to me: He on whom you see the Spirit descending from heaven and remaining on him, this is he who baptizes with the Holy Spirit’ (John 1:32–33). So the Holy Spirit was being prefigured, still as in shadows, coming down upon Christ in the form of fire and always remaining on him. For the fire of the altar never sleeps and never ceases at all. That the Spirit is likened to the nature of fire, the blessed Baptist also assures you when he says to the crowds of the Jews: ‘I baptize in water, but among you stands one whom you do not know, who comes after me, the strap of whose sandal I am not worthy to untie’ (John 1:26–27). And he said: ‘He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire’ (Matthew 3:11). For we have been baptized not into fire that the senses perceive, but in the Holy Spirit, who like fire melts away the defilement in souls. That is why it is also written of Christ: ‘Behold, he comes in like a refiner’s fire and like fullers’ soap; and he will sit refining and cleansing, as silver and as gold’ (Malachi 3:2–3). The fire of the altar, then, cannot be quenched. For the Holy Spirit has remained in Christ, even though the Spirit is in him by nature, inasmuch as he is God and is understood to be God. The law also called the fire the altar’s own (Leviticus 6:9). For even though the Only-begotten became man, and in the manner fitting for humanity is also said to have come to share in the Spirit, the Spirit is nonetheless both his and in him, and truly his own. But if someone chooses to apply this passage to each of those sanctified through faith in Christ, so that each is in some way already understood to be a divine altar, the reading is a profitable one. For it is fitting that holy men, who have dedicated their own life to Christ, be seen warm and fervent in the Spirit (Romans 12:11), and always so: not sinking into coldness through worldly pleasures, but rather rekindling the mind in holiness toward love of God and desire for virtue. For this is the manner of rational worship (Romans 12:1). This, then, is the meaning of the altar. But he adds a further command that is useful at the literal level as well. He says the ash must be carried out not by someone else, an outsider, that is, someone of another tribe, but rather by the service of those who have been sanctified (Leviticus 6:10–11). Observe how the law allows nothing that belongs to divine service to be thought trivial, or unworthy, as it were, of the priest’s own hands, so that he might hand it over to someone else who is not holy; for the holy things are not open to the unclean. The divine altar itself, too, is not to be touched.

PG 68.821. Palladius answers Cyril’s question at the end of section 20 (was not Emmanuel the altar, in type?). The subject of ἐᾷ (‘does not allow’) is unexpressed; rendered ‘the law’ from context. Leviticus references use English numbering: LXX Lev 6:2–6 = English 6:9–13. ‘Fire came down from heaven upon the altar’ is uncited: Lev 9:24 says the fire came out ‘from the Lord’; the heavenly origin may echo 2 Chronicles 7:1 or tradition, so no citation. ‘The law called the fire the altar’s own’ is a loose paraphrase, cited to Lev 6:9 (‘the fire of the altar’). John 1:32 as Cyril quotes it adds ‘in the form of a dove’ (ἐν εἴδει περιστερᾶς), language closer to Luke 3:22. Matthew 3:11 has the same words as Luke 3:16. Malachi 3:2–3 follows the LXX (‘herb of washers’, rendered ‘fullers’ soap’). ζέοντας τῷ Πνεύματι echoes Romans 12:11; λατρεία λογική picks up Romans 12:1, quoted at the end of section 20. The ash rule paraphrases Lev 6:10–11, where the priest himself removes the ash; ἀλλογενής (‘one of another race’) may echo Num 3:10 / 18:7, left uncited. The first words of col. 824 (ἐστι θυσιαστήριον, ‘is … altar’) are rendered at the end of this section so the sentence is whole; section 22 starts with the next sentence.

changes: Palladius reply: ‘and’ for γάρ tightened to a plain affirmation
ἀλλ’ εἶναι: dropped added verb ‘requires’; ‘fade and go away’ for ἀπανίστασθαι μαρανθέν
Doctrinal fix: μεμένηκε ἐν Χριστῷ is ‘remained in Christ’, not ‘on’; καθὸ rendered ‘inasmuch as’
ἀλλογενῶν: ‘an outsider’ for stiff ‘one of another race’
All 9 citations checked (Lev 6:12–13, 6:9, 6:10–11 English = LXX 6:2–6; John 1:32–33, 1:26–27; Matt 3:11; Mal 3:2–3 LXX; Rom 12:11, 12:1): correct
